task_1.title: Add DataArray to Dask DataFrame conversion support
task_1.description: Version 2023.5.0 adds a new public API for converting an xarray DataArray into a Dask DataFrame, enabling direct interoperability with chunked Dask-based tabular workflows. The feature preserves named data variables, supports explicit dimension ordering for row layout control, includes compatible coordinate columns in the tabular result, and rejects unsupported cases such as unnamed arrays or invalid dimension order declarations.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that users can convert a named DataArray directly into a Dask DataFrame for chunked tabular processing, with predictable column layout, dimension ordering, and validation of unsupported inputs.

expectation.grounded: Provide `DataArray.to_dask_dataframe(dim_order=None, set_index=False)` as a public conversion method that returns a `dask.dataframe.DataFrame`. The result should expose the DataArray's name as the data column, include relevant coordinate data as columns, honor a valid `dim_order` by flattening values in that transposed order, and delegate single-dimension index creation through `set_index` where supported. Calling the method on an unnamed `DataArray` must raise `ValueError`, and supplying a `dim_order` whose members do not exactly match the array dimensions must also raise `ValueError`.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to take a named xarray DataArray and obtain a Dask DataFrame that reflects the same data and coordinates in tabular form. They should be able to control the row ordering through dimension order selection, optionally request index-based output where the shape allows it, and receive clear failures for invalid conversion inputs rather than partial or ambiguous results.

constraints.grounded: The conversion must remain name-sensitive, preserving the DataArray name as the output data column and refusing unnamed arrays. It must not accept extra or missing dimensions in `dim_order`. Coordinate variables aligned to participating dimensions must remain observable in the output DataFrame. Existing semantics for value ordering must remain consistent with the specified dimension order and with the default order when none is provided.
constraints.conceptual: The feature must behave as a faithful tabular view of the original array rather than changing the data model. It should preserve meaningful labels and aligned coordinates, reject invalid shape or metadata configurations deterministically, and avoid regressions in ordering or column visibility across supported conversion cases.

behavior: A named `DataArray` can be converted directly to a `dask.dataframe.DataFrame` through `to_dask_dataframe()`.
The resulting DataFrame includes a data column named after the original `DataArray`.
When no explicit `dim_order` is given, values are flattened according to the default dimension ordering used by the conversion.
When `dim_order` is provided and matches the full set of array dimensions, the output row/value ordering follows that transposed dimension order.
Coordinates associated with one or more of the array dimensions are materialized as DataFrame columns when applicable.
If `set_index=True`, index-based output is only supported for cases compatible with Dask DataFrame indexing constraints.
If the `DataArray` has no name, conversion fails with `ValueError`.
If `dim_order` does not exactly match the DataArray dimensions, conversion fails with `ValueError`.
acceptance_criteria: When a named DataArray is converted with `to_dask_dataframe()`, it should return a Dask DataFrame containing a data column with the array name.
When the returned DataFrame is evaluated, its data values should match the original DataArray values expressed in tabular form.
When `dim_order` is set to a valid permutation of the DataArray dimensions, the DataFrame row ordering should reflect that dimension order.
When the DataArray has aligned coordinate variables on its dimensions, those coordinates should appear as columns in the converted DataFrame.
When `dim_order` includes extra dimensions, omits dimensions, or otherwise does not match the DataArray dimensions exactly, the conversion should raise `ValueError`.
When `to_dask_dataframe()` is called on an unnamed DataArray, it should raise `ValueError` instead of producing a DataFrame.
When index creation is requested for a supported single-dimension case, the DataFrame should expose that coordinate as its index.

task_3.title: Support array-preserving to_dict output
task_3.description: The upgrade expands xarray's dictionary serialization so callers can choose whether `Dataset.to_dict()` and `DataArray.to_dict()` return Python lists or preserve the underlying array-backed data objects. It also makes schema-only export explicit and includes variable-level encoding data when requested, improving interoperability and avoiding unnecessary materialization for array-based workflows.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that dictionary export for xarray datasets and data arrays supports preserving array-backed data without forcing conversion to Python lists, while keeping backward-compatible list output, schema-only export, and optional encoding export available through the public `to_dict()` API.

expectation.grounded: `xarray.Dataset.to_dict()` and `xarray.DataArray.to_dict()` must accept `data="array"` to return values using the underlying array type, `data="list"` to return Python lists, and `data=True` as a backward-compatible alias for list output. `data=False` must omit data payloads and return schema information only. When `encoding=True` is supplied, the serialized dictionary must include encoding metadata for the underlying variables so that `Dataset.from_dict()` and `DataArray.from_dict()` preserve observable encoding state on round-trip. Invalid `data` values must raise `ValueError`.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to choose between JSON-friendly list serialization and array-preserving serialization when exporting xarray objects to dictionaries. The export API should still support schema-only output, remain backward compatible for existing callers, and preserve requested encoding metadata through round-trip reconstruction.

constraints.grounded: Existing callers using `data=True` must continue to receive list-based data. `from_dict()` round-trips must remain valid for dictionaries produced with list output, array output, and schema-only output where applicable. Requesting array output should not force eager conversion to Python lists, and enabling encoding export must not drop variable encodings for coordinates or data variables.
constraints.conceptual: The new serialization mode must extend current behavior without breaking established exports. Different export modes should stay consistent with reconstruction behavior, avoid unnecessary data conversion, and preserve metadata fidelity when users opt in to encoding details.

behavior: `Dataset.to_dict()` and `DataArray.to_dict()` now support an explicit array-preserving export mode via `data="array"`.
List-based export remains available via `data="list"`, and `data=True` behaves like list output for backward compatibility.
Schema-only export via `data=False` continues to omit data values and return shape and dtype information instead.
When `encoding=True` is requested, the exported dictionary includes encoding metadata for serialized variables, including coordinates and data variables where relevant.
Dictionaries produced by these modes remain consumable by `Dataset.from_dict()` and `DataArray.from_dict()` for round-trip reconstruction.
Supplying an unsupported `data` option results in a `ValueError`.
acceptance_criteria: When a user calls `Dataset.to_dict(data="array")`, the returned dictionary should contain array-backed values instead of Python lists for dataset data and coordinates.
When a user calls `DataArray.to_dict(data="array")`, the returned dictionary should preserve the data array's underlying array type rather than converting values to lists.
When a user calls either API with `data="list"` or `data=True`, the returned dictionary should contain Python-list representations compatible with existing behavior.
When a user calls either API with `data=False`, the returned dictionary should exclude data payloads and expose schema information needed to describe the object structure.
When a user exports with `encoding=True` and reconstructs via `from_dict()`, the resulting object should preserve the original observable encoding metadata.
When a user reconstructs from dictionaries generated with list or array output, the resulting `Dataset` or `DataArray` should remain identical in data model content to the original object.
When a user passes an unsupported value to the `data` argument, the API should raise `ValueError`.

task_2.title: Add bit-shift operator support for xarray arrays and grouped data
task_2.description: The upgrade adds native left-shift and right-shift operator support to xarray integer data structures so users can apply `<<` and `>>` directly to DataArray, Dataset, Variable, and grouped or lazy-backed values with the same observable behavior they expect from NumPy-compatible integer operations.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that users can apply left-shift and right-shift binary operators directly to xarray integer data structures without dropping to raw NumPy arrays, and that these operations behave consistently across regular, grouped, and lazy-backed data while continuing to fail for unsupported input types.

expectation.grounded: xarray 2023.5.0 should support `<<` and `>>` on `xr.DataArray` values of integer type, and the operator support should also be available on `Dataset`, `Variable`, `DataArrayGroupBy`, and `DatasetGroupBy`. In-place variants should be available where the corresponding object already supports inplace binary operators. Results should follow the underlying NumPy or dask bit-shift semantics for integer operands, preserve normal xarray object identity rules for indexes and coordinates, and raise the underlying type error when shift operations are attempted on unsupported dtypes such as floating-point arrays.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to use bit shifting on xarray objects the same way they use other built-in arithmetic operators. Integer-based arrays and datasets should return shifted results directly, including for grouped and lazy data, while unsupported data types should still fail clearly instead of producing coerced or surprising results.

constraints.grounded: The added operator support must not change existing alignment, coordinate/index preservation, lazy evaluation compatibility, or groupby broadcasting behavior already used by xarray binary operations. Integer results should match NumPy-equivalent bit-shift outputs, and unsupported operand dtypes should continue to surface an error rather than silently casting.
constraints.conceptual: This feature should extend operator coverage without changing the established behavior of xarray objects. Existing metadata behavior, grouped computations, and lazy execution should remain consistent, and invalid inputs should still be rejected rather than implicitly altered.

behavior: Applying `<<` or `>>` to integer `DataArray` objects returns shifted `DataArray` results.
Applying `<<` or `>>` to integer `Dataset` and `Variable` objects returns shifted results that match NumPy integer bit-shift behavior.
Grouped xarray objects can participate in bit-shift operations with compatible shift values and produce the same grouped result as manually shifting each group.
Dask-backed variables support `<<` and `>>` with lazy results equivalent to eager integer variables.
In-place left-shift and right-shift operators are exposed for xarray object types that already support inplace binary operators.
Indexes and coordinate relationships that are normally preserved across binary operations remain preserved for bit-shift operations.
Attempting bit-shift operations on unsupported dtypes such as floating-point arrays raises the underlying type error instead of succeeding through implicit coercion.
acceptance_criteria: When a user applies `<<` to an integer `xr.DataArray`, it should return a shifted `DataArray` with values matching the equivalent integer NumPy operation.
When a user applies `>>` to an integer `xr.DataArray`, it should return a shifted `DataArray` with values matching the equivalent integer NumPy operation.
When a user applies `<<` or `>>` to integer `Variable` objects against scalars or integer arrays, the returned values should match NumPy bit-shift results.
When a user applies `<<` or `>>` to integer `Dataset` or grouped xarray objects, the result should match the output obtained by performing the same shift on each aligned group manually.
When a user performs bit-shift operations on dask-backed integer variables, the lazy result should be identical to the eager result after computation.
When a bit-shift operation is performed on an xarray object with preserved indexes or coordinates, those observable index relationships should remain intact in the result.
When a user attempts `<<` or `>>` on unsupported operand types such as floating-point data, the operation should raise a type error rather than return a shifted value.

task_4.title: Extend Python support window to align with NEP-29
task_4.description: The update changes the project's Python deprecation policy so supported Python releases remain available longer, restoring alignment with NEP-29. In practice, Python version removal is deferred by extending the policy window used to determine the minimum supported Python release.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Python version support is dropped only on the NEP-29-aligned schedule, so users on still-eligible Python releases are not forced to upgrade earlier than expected.

expectation.grounded: The project should apply a 30-month policy window for `python` when evaluating minimum supported versions, instead of 24 months, while leaving the existing 18-month `numpy` policy unchanged. The supported-Python calculation should recognize newer public Python minor releases including 3.9, 3.10, and 3.11 so the deprecation policy can be evaluated against current release history.
expectation.conceptual: Upgrading to this version should preserve compatibility with Python releases for the longer NEP-29-aligned support window. Users should only lose support for an older Python version once that version is old enough under the revised policy, rather than on the earlier schedule used before.

constraints.grounded: The change must be limited to Python support policy evaluation and must not shorten support windows for Python or alter the existing support policy for other dependencies such as `numpy`. The policy should remain based on Python minor-version release timing rather than patch-level churn.
constraints.conceptual: The update should avoid introducing unrelated dependency policy regressions. It should only delay Python deprecations to the intended schedule and keep the rest of the compatibility policy stable.

behavior: Python minimum-version eligibility is determined using a 30-month support window rather than 24 months.
Older Python versions remain supported for longer before being considered removable.
Evaluation of supported Python versions accounts for newer Python minor releases through 3.11.
Dependency support rules for non-Python packages remain unchanged by this update.
acceptance_criteria: When support policy is evaluated for Python, it should use the revised 30-month window.

When comparing this release with the previous policy, Python versions that would have been dropped solely because of the 24-month rule should remain supported until the NEP-29-aligned threshold is reached.
When determining current supported Python versions, releases including Python 3.9, 3.10, and 3.11 should be recognized by the policy logic.
When evaluating dependency support rules unrelated to Python, they should behave the same as before this update.

task_5.title: Speed up CFTime-backed .dt accessors without changing results
task_5.description: The update improves performance for xarray datetime accessors on CFTime-backed coordinates by preserving existing index objects instead of rebuilding them during .dt field extraction and rounding operations. User-visible behavior is intended to remain the same while common operations such as extracting date parts and rounding become faster on long time coordinates.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that datetime accessor operations on CFTime-backed coordinates remain behaviorally consistent while becoming faster for long time indexes, including date-part extraction and rounding-style operations.

expectation.grounded: For DataArray objects whose datetime-like coordinate is backed by a CFTimeIndex, .dt accessors should operate directly against the preserved index representation when available rather than forcing a new CFTimeIndex conversion first. Public .dt field accessors such as year and dayofyear, and rounding-style accessors such as floor, should continue returning xarray objects with the same dimensions, coordinates, and corresponding datetime-derived values as before.
expectation.conceptual: Datetime access on non-standard-calendar time coordinates should feel unchanged to users except for improved speed. Reading calendar fields and applying datetime rounding through .dt should produce the same observable results and object shape as prior versions.

constraints.grounded: The change must not alter the public .dt API surface or the returned xarray container structure for supported CFTime-backed inputs. Existing coordinate alignment, dimension names, and result dtypes expected by .dt field extraction and floor-like operations should be preserved, and behavior must remain compatible whether the underlying datetime values arrive as an index object or raw array-like data.
constraints.conceptual: The optimization must be non-breaking. It should preserve outputs, metadata shape, and normal datetime-access semantics while only reducing unnecessary work behind the scenes.

behavior: Accessing .dt fields on CFTime-backed coordinates should avoid observable regressions while completing more efficiently on long time ranges.
Calling .dt.year on CFTime-backed coordinates should continue to return the corresponding calendar year values in an xarray object with the original dimensional structure.
Calling .dt.dayofyear on CFTime-backed coordinates should continue to return the expected ordinal day values in an xarray object with the original dimensional structure.
Calling .dt.floor(freq) on CFTime-backed coordinates should continue to return rounded datetime values with the same xarray container semantics as before.
The accessor logic should support both existing CFTimeIndex inputs and equivalent non-index datetime arrays without changing user-facing results.
acceptance_criteria: When a DataArray uses a CFTime-backed time coordinate, accessing .dt.year should return the same year values and preserve the original dimensions and coordinates.
When a DataArray uses a CFTime-backed time coordinate, accessing .dt.dayofyear should return the same ordinal day values and preserve the original dimensions and coordinates.
When a CFTime-backed datetime coordinate is rounded with .dt.floor("D") or another supported frequency, it should return the same rounded timestamps and preserve the original xarray object shape.
When the datetime coordinate is already represented as a CFTimeIndex, .dt access should behave the same as with equivalent CFTime-backed values that are not already wrapped as an index.
On large CFTime-backed time coordinates, repeated .dt field extraction and rounding operations should show an improvement in runtime without requiring user code changes.

task_6.title: Handle read-only masked float arrays in xarray compatibility conversion
task_6.description: The upgrade fixes xarray's conversion of NumPy masked float arrays so masked values are safely materialized even when the source masked array is read-only. Operations that previously failed when a masked scalar or masked float array flowed through xarray now produce the expected promoted floating result with missing values represented consistently.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that xarray operations and constructors accept masked float inputs, including read-only masked arrays and masked scalars, without failing, and that masked elements are converted into the expected missing-value representation.

expectation.grounded: When xarray converts a NumPy `MaskedArray` through `as_compatible_data`, any input with a present mask must be handled by producing a compatible array value rather than mutating the source storage in place. For masked float data, masked positions should be represented using the promoted floating dtype and missing-value sentinel, and creating a `Variable` from `np.ma.masked` should succeed and yield a scalar missing value instead of raising a `ValueError` caused by read-only input.
expectation.conceptual: Masked inputs should work transparently in xarray. If a masked array or masked scalar is provided, xarray should return the same logical data with masked entries exposed as missing values, even when the original input cannot be written to.

constraints.grounded: Unmasked masked-array inputs should continue to convert to ordinary NumPy-compatible arrays without unnecessary behavioral change. Masked conversions must preserve the unmasked values, promote dtype when required to represent missing values, and avoid regressions in scalar and array construction paths that rely on `as_compatible_data`.
constraints.conceptual: The fix must not change the meaning of valid unmasked data. Only masked elements should become missing values, and existing successful conversions should keep behaving the same apart from no longer failing on read-only masked inputs.

behavior: Converting a masked float array with at least one masked element returns a compatible array where masked entries are exposed as missing values and unmasked entries are preserved.
The conversion succeeds even if the source `MaskedArray` has `writeable=False`.
Constructing an xarray `Variable` from `np.ma.masked` yields a scalar missing value with the expected floating dtype rather than raising `ValueError`.
Masked inputs follow the same observable semantics for scalar and non-scalar cases, so scalar comparisons involving masked values align with array-based behavior.
acceptance_criteria: When `as_compatible_data` receives a float `MaskedArray` with masked elements, it should return data where masked positions are missing values and unmasked positions retain their original values.
When the same masked float array is marked read-only, the conversion should still succeed and produce the same result.
When xarray constructs a `Variable` from `np.ma.masked`, it should produce a scalar missing value with floating dtype.
When masked data participates in xarray operations that trigger compatibility conversion, the operation should no longer fail solely because the masked input is read-only.

task_7.title: Fix subset groupby binary alignment
task_7.description: Upgrading to 2023.5.0 fixes incorrect alignment in xarray groupby binary operations when the grouped DataArray or Dataset is a subset of the categories present in the other operand. This restores correct results for workflows such as seasonal anomaly calculations performed on sliced data and keeps grouped operations consistent with equivalent explicit selection logic.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that groupby-based binary operations return correctly aligned results when the grouped data only contains a subset of group labels relative to the other operand, so sliced or filtered inputs produce the same values as equivalent explicit selection workflows.

expectation.grounded: In xarray 2023.5.0, binary operations involving GroupBy objects, including expressions such as `DataArray.groupby(...) - other`, should align the non-grouped operand to the grouped coordinate using only the labels present in the grouped object. When a grouped array is sliced to a subset of labels, operations against an aggregated or climatology-like operand must preserve the grouped object's shape and coordinates and yield the same values as computing the operation with an explicitly selected matching operand. GroupBy operations over multiple grouped arguments must continue to reject mismatched grouping definitions with `ValueError`.
expectation.conceptual: Grouped arithmetic should behave like normal label-aware arithmetic even after filtering or slicing the grouped data. If only some groups are present, the operation should use exactly those groups, produce correct values for those observations, and remain consistent with a manual align-then-operate workflow.

constraints.grounded: The fix must not expand subset inputs to an outer union of group labels during binary ops, must not introduce incorrect values for missing or dropped groups, and must preserve existing error behavior for operations that combine differently grouped GroupBy objects. Existing groupby and resample-style APIs should remain compatible, with no change to public method names or required arguments.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should correct the misalignment bug without changing the basic grouping model, without inventing extra groups, and without weakening validation for incompatible grouped operations.

behavior: Binary arithmetic between a subset GroupBy result and another labeled operand aligns using the subset's group labels rather than an outer label union.
Seasonal or categorical anomaly calculations on sliced data produce the expected zero or matching anomaly values when the reference data already contains the same labels.
The result keeps the subset input's observation dimension and associated coordinates instead of being distorted by labels that are absent from the grouped subset.
Operations involving multiple GroupBy inputs still require equivalent grouping definitions and continue to raise `ValueError` when they differ.
acceptance_criteria: When a time series is sliced to a single month and subtracted from a month-indexed climatology using `groupby("time.month")`, it should produce the same result as subtracting the explicitly selected climatology for that month.

When grouped data is a subset of the labels present in the other operand, performing a binary operation should return values only for the subset observations and should not misalign them to other labels.
When the subset and reference values correspond exactly, the grouped binary operation should return zero anomalies rather than non-zero artifacts.
When two GroupBy operands are not grouped the same way, the operation should continue to fail with `ValueError` rather than silently proceeding.

task_8.title: Align flox-backed groupby reduction semantics with standard xarray behavior
task_8.description: The upgrade corrects an inconsistency introduced when groupby reductions are executed through flox. Grouped `sum` and `prod` now produce the same observable results as the non-flox path for all-NaN groups when `min_count` is omitted or set to `None`, and unsupported use of `min_count` on reductions such as `mean` continues to fail consistently.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that grouped reductions behave consistently across execution backends after upgrading, especially for `sum` and `prod` on groups containing only missing values, and ensure unsupported `min_count` usage still raises an error instead of changing reduction semantics.

expectation.grounded: For `DataArray.groupby(...)` reductions executed with `xr.set_options(use_flox=True)`, `sum` and `prod` must match the observable results from `xr.set_options(use_flox=False)` when `min_count` is omitted or explicitly `None`, including groups whose values are all `NaN`. `min_count` remains a supported argument only for `sum` and `prod`; passing `min_count` to reductions such as `mean` must raise `TypeError` regardless of whether flox is used.
expectation.conceptual: Users should see the same grouped aggregation results regardless of whether the optional flox acceleration path is enabled. Missing-data handling for additive and multiplicative group reductions should follow the library's standard defaults, and invalid reduction arguments should continue to fail predictably.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the public reduction contract for `GroupBy.mean` or other reductions that do not accept `min_count`. Do not introduce backend-specific differences between flox-enabled and non-flox groupby results for `sum` and `prod` under the same `skipna` and `min_count` inputs. Existing groupby arithmetic behavior must remain valid.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade must remove backend inconsistencies without widening APIs or altering unrelated grouped operations. Unsupported options must still be rejected, and previously correct grouped arithmetic behavior must not regress.

behavior: Grouped `sum` on an all-NaN group returns the same value with flox enabled as with flox disabled when `min_count` is not provided.
Grouped `prod` on an all-NaN group follows the same cross-backend consistency rule as `sum`.
When `min_count=None` is supplied to grouped `sum` or `prod`, it is treated as the default reduction behavior rather than producing flox-specific missing results.
When `min_count=1` is supplied to grouped `sum` or `prod`, flox-backed and non-flox executions remain aligned.
Passing `min_count` to grouped reductions that do not support it, such as `mean`, raises `TypeError` with or without flox enabled.
Grouped binary arithmetic on sliced time-based groups continues to preserve correct alignment semantics and yields the expected result.
acceptance_criteria: When a grouped dataset contains a label whose members are all missing values, calling `groupby(...).sum()` with flox enabled should produce the same result as calling it with flox disabled.
When the same grouped dataset is reduced with `groupby(...).prod()`, flox-enabled and flox-disabled execution should return identical results for all groups, including all-missing groups.
Given `min_count=None`, calling grouped `sum` or `prod` should behave the same as the default call and should not change results only because flox is enabled.
Given `min_count=1`, calling grouped `sum` or `prod` should return the same observable result in both flox-enabled and flox-disabled modes.
When `min_count` is passed to `groupby(...).mean(...)`, the operation should raise `TypeError` regardless of backend selection.
When performing grouped arithmetic against month-based climatology on a sliced time selection, the result should remain correctly aligned and match the expected zero-anomaly outcome.

task_9.title: Generalize xarray chunked-array support beyond dask
task_9.description: xarray 2023.5.0 adds experimental support for chunked array libraries beyond dask by introducing a chunk-manager abstraction and exposing backend-selection options on chunking, loading, creation, and storage APIs. Users can choose a registered chunked array implementation, and chunk-aware operations now dispatch through the detected manager instead of assuming dask-specific behavior.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that xarray users can work with registered chunked array backends other than dask through the same high-level chunking and I/O workflows. Ensure that chunk-aware operations select the appropriate backend automatically for supported arrays and reject unsupported or mixed chunked-array types with clear failures.

expectation.grounded: xarray should provide experimental chunk-manager extensibility through `xr.namedarray.parallelcompat.ChunkManagerEntrypoint`, with manager selection and backend-specific argument forwarding available on public APIs including `Dataset.chunk`, `DataArray.chunk`, `Variable.chunk`, `open_dataset`, `open_dataarray`, `open_zarr`, `full_like`, `zeros_like`, `ones_like`, and `to_zarr`. The `chunked_array_type` option should allow choosing a registered manager by name, defaulting to `dask` when available, otherwise to the single registered manager. `from_array_kwargs` should be forwarded when creating chunked arrays, and `chunkmanager_store_kwargs` should be forwarded when storing chunked arrays. Operations that compute, rechunk, unify chunks, apply gufuncs, run blockwise/map_blocks logic, or perform chunk-aware reductions should dispatch via the detected `ChunkManagerEntrypoint` for the array type rather than assuming dask arrays only.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to select a supported chunked execution backend for xarray data loading, chunk conversion, array creation, and zarr writing, while existing dask-based usage continues to work. Once data is backed by a supported chunked array type, xarray should carry out chunked computations through that backend consistently across common lazy operations instead of treating dask as the only valid parallel engine.

constraints.grounded: Manager resolution must fail when the requested `chunked_array_type` is not registered, when no chunked arrays are present for backend detection, when no registered manager recognizes the chunked array type, or when multiple chunked array types are mixed in the same operation. Non-chunked in-memory inputs such as NumPy arrays and Python scalars must not interfere with chunk-manager detection. Existing `dask`-specific arguments remain accepted where exposed, but conflicting values passed both directly and via `from_array_kwargs` must be rejected. Chunk-shape warnings about splitting stored chunks should remain applicable in backend-neutral terms.
constraints.conceptual: The feature must preserve current behavior for ordinary in-memory arrays and for dask-backed arrays, while preventing ambiguous backend selection and unsupported mixtures of lazy array types. Backend selection should be explicit or reliably inferred, and invalid combinations should fail rather than silently choosing the wrong execution engine.

behavior: Calling chunking APIs with `chunked_array_type` selects the named registered chunk manager for creating or rechunking lazy arrays.
If no manager is specified, xarray prefers dask when it is available; otherwise it uses the only registered chunk manager.

`full_like`, `zeros_like`, and `ones_like` can now create chunked outputs based on existing chunked inputs or explicit chunking options, with backend-specific creation kwargs forwarded through `from_array_kwargs`.
`open_dataset`, `open_dataarray`, and `open_zarr` can coerce loaded arrays into the selected chunked backend instead of always targeting dask semantics.
Chunked `load` and `compute` operations execute through the detected backend manager's multi-array compute path.

Chunk-aware internals such as `apply_ufunc(..., dask='parallelized')`, `unify_chunks`, interpolation, lazy elementwise string/coding helpers, and first/last reductions operate against the detected chunk manager rather than hard-coding dask-only helpers.
Writing chunked arrays via `to_zarr` forwards storage execution to the selected chunk manager and accepts backend-specific store kwargs through `chunkmanager_store_kwargs`.
Operations that encounter mixed chunked-array implementations or an unknown manager raise errors instead of proceeding with implicit cross-backend behavior.
acceptance_criteria: When a user calls `Dataset.chunk`, `DataArray.chunk`, or `Variable.chunk` with a supported `chunked_array_type`, the result should use that chunked backend for newly created or rechunked lazy arrays.

When a supported chunked array backend is already present and the user calls `full_like`, `zeros_like`, or `ones_like`, the returned object should preserve lazy chunked behavior or honor the explicitly requested chunking/backend options.
When a user opens data with `open_dataset`, `open_dataarray`, or `open_zarr` and supplies a supported `chunked_array_type`, xarray should return lazily chunked arrays managed by that backend.
When chunked arrays participate in compute-heavy xarray operations, xarray should route execution through the matching backend manager and not require dask-specific array types.
When no chunk manager matches a requested backend name or a chunked array type, the operation should raise an error.
When an operation mixes different chunked array implementations in the same call, it should raise an error rather than silently combining them.
When non-chunked scalars or NumPy arrays are included alongside a supported chunked array, backend detection should still select the supported chunked backend.
When backend-specific kwargs are supplied for array creation or storage, they should be forwarded through the corresponding manager interface, and conflicting duplicate kwargs should be rejected.
